per_pillar_sell_caveats.buyer_orientation: Low real rates → higher sub-score (favorable to buy).
per_pillar_sell_caveats.seller_caveat: Falling real rates are a HOLDING tailwind, not a sell trigger. Rising real rates weaken the buy case but also erode the marginal seller's incentive symmetrically only if they need dollars; long-term holders are typically indifferent to real rates in the short run.

per_pillar_sell_caveats.buyer_orientation: Price below trend / cheap in real terms → higher sub-score.
per_pillar_sell_caveats.seller_caveat: The valuation sub-signal INVERTS cleanly for sellers: real price at the top of its long-run distribution is precisely the condition under which historical forward real returns were weakest (Erb-Harvey), i.e., a defensible sell condition. Trend momentum inverts too: a negative 12m return often continued; selling into strength (positive trend, above 12m MA) has historically been a better price than selling into weakness.

per_pillar_sell_caveats.buyer_orientation: CB accumulation / ETF inflows → higher sub-score.
per_pillar_sell_caveats.seller_caveat: Physical retail sellers face the LFP absorber directly. In periods of strong CB accumulation (2022-2024), dealer bids are firm and the physical sell workflow is smooth. When CB demand recedes, physical bids widen (worse execution). Effect is on friction, not directionality.
For a USD-quoted physical seller, dollar direction cancels out: the numeraire caveat applies symmetrically. Non-USD sellers should read the pillar in their own currency's dollar cross.

per_pillar_sell_caveats.buyer_orientation: COT MM net %OI at LOW percentile → higher sub-score (washed-out longs).
per_pillar_sell_caveats.seller_caveat: High COT MM net %OI (crowded long) inverts cleanly for sellers: it has historically preceded washouts. This is the pillar with the strongest sell-side signal at percentile extremes.

per_pillar_sell_caveats.buyer_orientation: High GVZ → LOW sub-score (poor entry conditions).
per_pillar_sell_caveats.seller_caveat: High implied vol raises option premia and the bid/ask on physical spreads; execution costs rise for BOTH sides. Not a directional sell trigger.

per_pillar_sell_caveats.buyer_orientation: High retail premiums → LOW sub-score (worse all-in price for buyers).
per_pillar_sell_caveats.seller_caveat: High retail premiums are directly BETTER for physical sellers: dealer bids sit closer to spot when their sell-side inventory is tight, and cash-buyers of jewelry/coins bid harder. Cost argument, incontestable. This pillar has the cleanest buyer-vs-seller inversion in the entire instrument.
